source: creator-locked 11-slide copy plus creator-directed day-in-the-life visual route on 2026-07-30
guardrail_role: engineering blocks only hard failures after the creator-directed visual route
preservation_rule: Preserve the exact copy and the recognisable office, dining-table, shared-stress, cushion-fight, remote-check-in, separate-home, and next-morning habit scenes. Never restore the rejected broken-key route.

concept.title: Not Married Yet, Already Us
concept.human_truth: Long before vows, two people begin behaving like a unit through automatic habits, shared decisions, shared stress, real friction, and concern that survives irritation.
concept.emotional_arc: unofficial habits -> mutual decisions -> one problem becomes shared stress -> equal friction -> care survives without erasing anger -> separate homes, already an us
concept.visual_system: A warm day-in-the-life relationship sitcom across an office, dining table, living room, corridor, and two separate homes, with a next-morning habit match cut.

visual_setup: Native Instagram post carousel only, 1080x1440. Premium Observational Intimacy watercolor-and-ink on neutral warm ivory paper with visible grain, never yellow, sepia, tan, or parchment. Each slide is a large instantly readable lived situation, not a symbolic prop puzzle. Slides 1-2 are the same office morning; slides 3-10 cover the same evening and night; slide 11 returns to the morning lobby/cafe in new reference-anchored clothes. Preserve clean upper-middle negative space for exact integrated handwritten copy and the tiny top-right @a.storyof.two brandmark. No random text, phone UI, speech bubbles, decorative hearts, wedding symbols, reflections, duplicate figures, generic romantic embraces, broken keys, injured thumbs, tissue dabs, or repaired locks.

slides.copy:
We’re not married yet.
But try telling that to our habits.
slides.visual: Morning outside a contemporary office lobby cafe. Aachu casually straightens Zuv's slightly twisted office ID lanyard with her right hand while Zuv simultaneously passes her the takeaway coffee he already ordered with his left. Both keep walking rather than posing; their free arms, wrists, hands, coffee, and lanyard remain fully owned and separate. The reciprocal actions occupy the lower two-thirds beneath generous clean text space.
slides.emotion: automatic familiarity with light morning warmth
slides.cta_intent: make partners recognise the tiny routines that become an us before vows
slides.pose: Medium-wide three-quarter two-shot at equal camera depth; Zuv only two inches taller. Aachu reaches to the lanyard without leaning into him; Zuv extends the coffee without stopping their forward motion.
slides.wardrobe: Morning outfits anchored to the selected identity references: Zuv in his white/off-white office top with grey trousers and visible ID lanyard; Aachu in a light casual top with blue denim and simple jewellery.
slides.props: One plain takeaway coffee cup with no label or writing; one simple office ID card whose face and text stay unreadable; no extra cup, bag, phone, or sign text.
slides.background: Airy office-lobby cafe entrance with understated glass, stone, and one soft plant mass fading into ivory paper; no readable signage, logos, reflections, or background people.
slides.continuity_lock: Setup for slide 11's next-morning match cut. Exactly two people and four traceable hands. Coffee passes from Zuv to Aachu while Aachu fixes Zuv's lanyard.

slides.copy:
Every plan starts with:
“Ek minute, usse poochna padega.”
slides.visual: Inside Zuv's office break area, exactly two friends or colleagues face him while proposing a plan. One sits forward and one stands beside the table, both visibly waiting mid-conversation. Zuv gives them a natural one-minute palm with his free hand, turns slightly aside, and lifts his phone to his ear to call Aachu before agreeing.
slides.cta_intent: make the viewer recognise the reflex to consult the person who already feels official
slides.pose: Over-the-friends medium shot. Zuv remains the clear focal person with phone at one ear and the other palm gently raised; the colleagues react with amused patience, not mockery.
slides.wardrobe: Same office-morning Zuv outfit and lanyard as slide 1. The two colleagues wear simple muted office-casual clothes that do not compete with him.
slides.props: One plain phone with its screen hidden, one small office table, and two unlabelled cups; no laptops, documents, signs, UI, or readable badges.
slides.background: Sparse office break area with neutral daylight and restrained furniture fading into the paper; no extra people, portraits, reflections, brand names, or office signage.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly three people: Zuv plus two colleagues. Zuv has two visible traceable hands; colleagues' visible hands remain attached and idle. The action must read as making a call, not checking work information or asking permission.

slides.copy:
Every small decision becomes
a two-person meeting.
slides.visual: That evening, Aachu and Zuv sit opposite each other at a dining table converted into an absurdly serious meeting. Papers, two notebooks, an open laptop with no visible UI, pens, a small blank calendar, and two mugs surround just two tiny curtain-fabric swatches at the centre. Both lean in and point at the swatches with concentrated boardroom seriousness.
slides.cta_intent: make couples recognise how tiny choices become formal joint decisions
slides.pose: High three-quarter near-overhead wide view. Aachu and Zuv occupy opposite sides of the table at equal visual weight, each using one pointing hand while the other rests visibly and naturally.
slides.wardrobe: Begin the same-evening continuity used through slide 10: Aachu in the black outer layer over a black top with blue jeans; Zuv in the off-white zip top and grey trousers, all anchored to selected identity references.
slides.props: Two small plain fabric swatches, several blank or abstract-mark papers, two notebooks, one open laptop with dark unreadable screen, pens, one blank calendar, and two unlabelled mugs. No readable words, numbers, charts, brands, or decorative signs.
slides.background: Specific lived dining nook with a wood table, two occupied chairs, one sideboard edge, and soft evening lamp light; no extra chairs staged like people, portraits, or clutter.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. The two tiny swatches are the visible decision target; paperwork exaggerates the meeting without becoming random decoration. Same evening wardrobe continues through slide 10.

slides.visual: Later in the same home, Zuv sits alone in the dominant foreground at the coffee table, reading one troubling work document beside the same laptop. One hand presses his forehead while the other owns the single document. Aachu has just entered at the far edge of the room and stops when she notices his face; she does not touch the problem or begin solving it yet.
slides.cta_intent: establish that the problem starts with one person before it spreads
slides.pose: Tight single-person-biased medium shot from coffee-table height. Zuv fills most of the lower frame; Aachu is a clear but secondary edge reaction with both feet planted and hands lowered.
slides.props: One work document with abstract non-text marks, one laptop with no readable UI, and one pen. No phones, keys, cushions in hands, duplicate papers, or invented labels.
slides.background: Same living-dining home, now framed toward the sofa and coffee table under motivated warm lamp light; no extra people, reflections, portraits, or signage.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people, but Zuv and the single document dominate. Aachu only notices. The same document and laptop move to the centre of slide 5.

slides.visual: The same work document and laptop now sit centred on the coffee table. Aachu and Zuv occupy opposite ends of the sofa in mirrored thinking postures, both leaning forward with one elbow on a knee and one hand near the forehead, staring at the same single problem. Their matching tension shows that his worry has entered both heads.
slides.cta_intent: prove that one person's worry becomes shared emotional labour
slides.pose: Symmetrical wide frontal shot. Both faces remain readable, feet planted, bodies separate, and natural two-inch height relationship preserved while seated.
slides.props: The same one document, laptop, and pen centred on the coffee table. Two sofa cushions remain in their normal positions, setting up slide 6 without being handled yet.
slides.background: Same sofa, coffee table, lamp, and room geography as slide 4, with restrained lived detail and clean upper text space.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. The single problem remains visually singular and centred. Their mirrored stress must not read as an existing fight yet. Sofa and cushion positions become the incoming state for slide 6.

slides.visual: The shared stress has erupted into a real cushion fight across the same living room. Aachu stands screen-left just after releasing one cushion from her right hand; that cushion is clearly airborne between them while her left hand grips a second cushion at her side. Zuv stands screen-right with both hands visibly gripping a third cushion, torso twisted and ready to throw it back. Both have tight brows, tense shoulders, planted feet, and open mouths mid-argument with no smile, laugh, playful bounce, or romantic energy. The work document has shifted on the coffee table but remains intact and owned by no hand.
slides.cta_intent: show that the relationship includes real conflict rather than decorative compatibility
slides.pose: Low wide action angle showing both full bodies and the gap between them. Aachu and Zuv carry equal visual weight; no cushion hides a face, torso, wrist, hand, or foot.
slides.props: Exactly three cushions: one airborne from Aachu, one held by Aachu's left hand, and one held by both of Zuv's hands. The same laptop, document, pen, sofa, and coffee table remain. No broken objects, weapons, phones, keys, tissue, or extra cushion.
slides.background: Same living-room geography as slide 5, now activated by shifted cushions and slightly displaced papers; solid furniture boundaries remain continuous and separate from both bodies.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people, four traceable arms, four traceable hands, and three cushions. Aachu's right hand is open after release; her left grips one cushion. Zuv's two hands grip one cushion. One airborne cushion stays fully separated from faces and limbs. Expressions and posture must read as genuinely angry, not playful pillow fighting.

slides.copy:
Then five minutes later:
“Ghar pahunch ke text karna.”
slides.visual: Five minutes later in the same messy living room, the three cushions remain scattered and the work document still sits askew. Zuv is at the open front door putting on one shoe and lifting his office bag to leave. Aachu remains beside the sofa with stiff shoulders and averted gaze, calling the line after him without approaching. Zuv pauses at the threshold to hear her but keeps his torso and leading foot oriented outward.
slides.cta_intent: show care surviving immediately after a proper fight
slides.pose: Wide inside-looking-out view. Aachu stays inside near the sofa; Zuv is at the threshold in a stable shoe-on posture with no crouched or twisted anatomy and no step back toward her.
slides.wardrobe: Same evening outfits as slides 3-6; Zuv now carries the same office bag associated with his separate workday.
slides.props: The same three cushions scattered in clear positions, same work document and laptop, one office bag, and Zuv's shoes. No helmet, key fragment, tissue, thumb injury, phone UI, or new decorative object.
slides.background: Same living-room geography opening naturally toward one front door and corridor; no central split-screen divider, extra doorway, reflection, or background person.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Fight residue from slide 6 remains visible. Zuv's movement is outward only. He pauses to hear Aachu but does not return, reach inward, or soften into a smile.

slides.visual: From the corridor behind Zuv, he continues walking away with tight shoulders, office bag at his side, and an unsmiling three-quarter profile. Through the open doorway behind him, Aachu sharply picks up one fallen cushion and turns her torso away. The corridor ahead, both of Zuv's feet, and his hips all point away from the apartment; neither person approaches the other.
slides.cta_intent: hold the anger on screen so the coming care does not erase it
slides.pose: Long corridor wide shot. Zuv is foreground moving outward; Aachu is smaller but readable inside the open doorway with one owned cushion and no reaching gesture.
slides.props: Zuv's office bag and one of the same fight cushions in Aachu's hands; the other two cushions remain visible inside. No keys, tissue, phone screen, sign, or extra bag.
slides.background: One continuous corridor leading away from the same open apartment door, with restrained wall and floor lines fading into neutral ivory paper.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Zuv moves only outward; the door and Aachu remain behind him. No turn back, return, inward reach, reunion, smile, or left-right axis flip.

slides.visual: Later, Aachu sits alone on the same sofa with the room only partly reset. Two cushions have been returned but one remains on the floor, and the work document is still askew. Her brows remain tight and her posture stays guarded, yet she presses her phone to her ear after placing a live call to check whether Zuv is okay. She does not smile.
slides.cta_intent: make the remote check-in the clearest proof that care survives friction
slides.pose: Intimate side-medium single of Aachu with face, phone hand, free hand, and guarded shoulders readable; no cramped curl, tearful melodrama, or reconciliation pose.
slides.wardrobe: Same evening Aachu outfit as slides 3-8.
slides.props: One plain phone with screen hidden, the same three cushions in changed positions, same document and laptop. No second phone, tissue, bandage, heart sticker, call UI, or readable text.
slides.background: Same living room under slightly later night light, visibly only partly reset after the fight; no Zuv, reflection, portrait, silhouette, or extra person.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly one person: Aachu. Phone is pressed to her ear in a live-call posture. Fight residue stays visible. The matching answered-call posture continues on slide 10.

slides.visual: Zuv has reached his own separate front door at night and answers the same call with his phone pressed to one ear while his other hand unlocks his door. He stands alone with his office bag, expression softened only slightly, making the separate-home reality visible without wedding symbols or a staged ring close-up.
slides.cta_intent: show separate official lives connected by already-shared emotional reflexes
slides.pose: Quiet medium-wide exterior landing shot. Zuv is upright in three-quarter view with one phone hand, one key hand, office bag hanging cleanly from one shoulder, and complete traceable silhouette.
slides.wardrobe: Same evening Zuv outfit as slides 3-8.
slides.props: One plain phone with screen hidden, one ordinary key in the lock, and the same office bag. No broken key, ring emphasis, wedding object, tissue, bandage, duplicate phone, or readable sign.
slides.background: A clearly different simple home threshold from slide 7, using distinct door colour and landing details while preserving neutral ivory paper and no readable number or nameplate.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly one person: Zuv. Matching phone-to-ear action follows slide 9. His separate home must read clearly; this is arrival at his own door, not a return to Aachu's home.

slides.copy:
Shaadi abhi baaki hai.
Par “hum” toh kab ke ban chuke hain.
slides.visual: The next morning returns to the office-lobby cafe geography from slide 1 in new reference-anchored clothes. Without discussion, Aachu brings Zuv's forgotten office ID card in her right hand while Zuv slides her already-ordered coffee toward her with his left; they meet mid-step and exchange both things at once. Their expressions carry only a small lived-in recognition, not a romantic pose or full reconciliation scene.
slides.cta_intent: land the sendable truth that the habits became an us before the vows
slides.pose: Wider match-cut to slide 1 with equal camera depth, natural two-inch height difference, both faces readable, and both reciprocal actions fully separated.
slides.wardrobe: New next-morning outfits selected from the same identity reference bundle; do not repeat the evening living-room clothes.
slides.props: One plain coffee cup and one office ID card with unreadable face and text. No rings, flowers, garlands, paired keys, wedding portrait, sign, or extra cup.
slides.background: Same office-lobby cafe entrance as slide 1 with changed morning foot traffic implied only through light and chair position; no background people, signage, reflections, or logos.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people and four traceable hands. Slide 1's lanyard-and-coffee habit returns with changed meaning: Aachu brings the forgotten ID while Zuv brings the coffee. No embrace or wedding cue.

copy.caption_recommended: No vows yet. Bas habits ne thoda jaldi decide kar liya. 🤍
copy.caption_alt: Officially, not married. Unofficially, every plan, problem, fight and check-in already comes in plural.
